answers.answer: 1. Each player starts with 25 money. 2. Take 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it. 3. Draw 8 Zoo cards and keep 4; discard the other 4 face up. 4. Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 5. Put side I of all five Action cards into slots; Animals goes in slot 1 and the other four are random. 6. Start appeal is staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup B–F: 25 money; 1 active/3 inactive workers; 8 draw, keep 4; draw 2 scoring cards; Animals in leftmost slot; Appeal track stagger.

answers.answer: 1. Put 3 Base Conservation Projects face up below the Association board in 2- and 3-player games, and 4 in a 4-player game. 2. In a 2-player game only, block the left, middle and right reward levels on the respective three face-up projects, and block the three spaces in the donation area's left column; these are unavailable to both players. 3. After all players choose their hands, reveal the six display cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c: four cards in 4-player, otherwise three; 2-player blocked levels/donation spaces. Personal setup G reveals display after hands.

answers.answer: 1. After using a slot-4 card, remove it; shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right; put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before performing it; each X-token spent beforehand adds +1 strength and returns to supply, while X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. 3. You may spend any number, but may hold at most 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an after-finishing effect only after the action is complete, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: card rotation; X-tokens; “strength before performing”; “after finishing” effects.

answers.answer: 1. You may not do nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal. 2. Instead, choose an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right. 3. The action's strength and upgrade state do not matter, and you cannot take this alternative if you already have 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn; X-TOKEN action: take exactly 1, rotate card, unavailable at 5 tokens.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches its final space, ignore additional steps beyond it. 2. The player who reaches it gains 1 X-token. 3. Finish the current turn, then take the break for everyone. 4. After the break the token returns to the start space and play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: The Break track: last space, 1 X-token, excess ignored, break after current turn; break procedure resets token.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then choose deck draw by the strength table or, at strength 5+, snap exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation instead of drawing. 2. Cards II also advances it 2 spaces, then allows deck draws and/or display draws within reputation range in any order; at strength 5 the table allows 4 cards and discard 1. Its snap is available from strength 3 and takes exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation, instead of a deck draw. 3. Display cards taken during a turn are replenished only at turn end. 4. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the limit only at breaks (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university).
answers.evidence: CARDS action and Special Rules: both sides advance 2; snap thresholds and exception; display timing; hand limit at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. Your reputation counter defines the display range: the folder matching your counter and all lower-numbered folders are in range. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires the upgraded Cards action. 3. At space 15, further reputation leaves the counter at 15 and grants 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: range definition, 10+ requires Cards II, overflow at 15; discard pile rule.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building of size up to action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical buildings in one action. 2. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. 3. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch a building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty map spaces; cannot extend off-map, overlap, or cover water/rock. Spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. 5. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately increases appeal by 1, once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: side limits and cost; placement rules; spacing; pavilion appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo; the Petting Zoo is size 3. 2. Build II additionally permits one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary (each size 5). Each zoo may have at most one of each special-enclosure type; the supply has four tiles of each type. 3. Build cannot build unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. 4. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal, and restricted spaces require Build II unless another effect provides an applicable exception.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table; Build II; unique buildings only via Sponsor; full map reward.

answers.answer: 1. Yes: bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that action. 2. Pay for each item before receiving that item's own benefits; for example, an animal's full cost must be paid before its play-generated money. 3. Immediate effects resolve at their stated point, while after-finishing effects wait until the entire action and card movement are complete. 4. If multiple effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens section says earlier bonuses may be used later and each item paid first; Animal effect timing; simultaneous effects rule.

answers.answer: 1. To play an animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, and provide legal housing and terrain adjacency. 2. A partner zoo on the animal's continent discounts 3 money per continent icon printed on the animal, so two such icons reduce cost by 6. 3. A non-Petting-Zoo animal can occupy an empty standard enclosure meeting its minimum size; flip the entire enclosure to occupied. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Aviary; add one supply player token per indicated special-space requirement and never flip the special enclosure. 4. Meet the printed water/rock adjacency requirement for the chosen enclosure, counting distinct adjacent hexes; repeated edges to one terrain hex count once. 5. Appeal and other normal effects resolve after housing; ordinary effects are immediate and after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement finish.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: conditions, cost discount per icon, housing, terrain, and effect timing.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits display animals within reputation range as well as hand animals, in any mix allowed by the animal capacity. 2. Pay an additional cost equal to the card's display folder number; do not refill the display until turn end. 3. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so its increased range applies to that action. 4. Animals II also permits animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS Side II: display, folder cost, optional reputation first, upgrade-conditioned animals.

answers.answer: 1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move corresponding eligible animals into that newly built enclosure; move all that fit, deciding separately for each. 2. The new special enclosure must satisfy each animal's water/rock adjacency and have free capacity; mark each animal's indicated capacity with that many supply player tokens. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements, including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even the size requirement, flip none.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure: only immediately at construction; capacity; smallest-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly 1 task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is at most action strength. 3. Each task needs an active worker; if you already have 1 worker on that task, place 2 workers to repeat it; with 3 of your workers there, you cannot do it again before the break. 4. Other players' workers on the task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: listed strengths; side I/II; repeat-worker rule; other players do not matter.

answers.answer: 1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest empty matching spaces on your map, taking any printed covered-space bonus immediately. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents and are limited to 4, with the third and fourth requiring Association II. 3. Partner zoos provide their continent icon and reduce matching animal costs by 3 per continent icon on each animal. 4. Universities provide research icons and their own printed reputation award; only the hand-limit university raises hand limit from 3 to 5. University reputation and hand-limit symbol are not zoo icons.
answers.evidence: Association task details; Your zoo map; University tiles table.

answers.answer: 1. Association project work may support a project already in play, or add a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II also permits a new project from the in-range display, paying its folder number. 2. A support requires a fulfilled, unoccupied reward condition; each level can hold one player's token total, and normally you may support a particular project only once. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your zoo map, place it on that condition, then gain its reward and uncover/take the map bonus immediately (before or after the project reward, your choice); recurring income repeats each break. 4. New cards enter leftmost above the Association board; if over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return its tokens to owners' supplies, while map bonuses remain activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work: enter play, overflow, support limits/procedure; Association II display source.

answers.answer: 1. Match the animal's printed standard-enclosure size category, not necessarily an exact number: 2− accepts size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. 2. Lose only that animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier earned effects. 3. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; later support of one already in play does not. 4. If the animal could use a special enclosure and its required special-enclosure tokens can be removed, remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or fall back to the smallest meeting size alone, or flip none if none meets size. 5. Special-enclosure tokens/capacity do not determine the release category.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects: size categories; losses retained; new-card reputation; token removal and standard-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and its conditions are met, or takes the money option. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards, with strength +1 at least the sum of their levels; X-tokens may raise strength above 5. Cards may come from hand and/or the in-range display, with each display card costing its folder number; refill only at turn end. 3. Resolve cards one by one, completing each card's instant effects before the next and deferring after-finishing effects until the action ends. 4. If choosing the break-track money option, Sponsors I takes money equal to strength even if fewer steps remain before the end; Sponsors II takes twice that amount.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: side I/II level rules, display cost/timing, effect order, money option.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock one of each available partner-zoo continent/university kind (except kinds owned by all players); discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university, checked only at breaks. 3. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. 4. When multiple players take display cards during income, resolve clockwise beginning with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), and refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income; display-card ordering and refill during income.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade one Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile. At 10, the first player to reach/pass it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before final scoring. 2. Check the end trigger at the end of your turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained on another player's turn waits until the affected player's turn end or a break unless another player triggers first. 3. If triggered at a turn end, finish that turn and each other player gets one more turn; if triggered during a break, every player gets one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card grants at most 4 conservation. 5. VP = your Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter; highest positive total wins, with most supported projects as tiebreak, then tied players share.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: milestones, end trigger, final turn sets, cap, formula and tiebreak.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random face-up tile on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two at 5 and two at 8; do not use the two yellow icon spaces and return the other 5 tiles to the box. 2. If a component runs out, use a suitable substitute; physical supply alone does not prohibit a legal play, though explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup step 2; Component supply edge case.

answers.answer: 1. For advanced maps, take 2 random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or reveal player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse play order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk is overlaid by a kiosk tile as a reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced-map selection; Map A ability.

answers.answer: 1. Place the 7 player tokens on the designated spaces along the left edge of your zoo map; these support conservation projects and uncover bonuses when removed. 2. Hire inactive workers from the lowest space upward. 3. Some maps reward conservation points for hiring your last worker; Map A's second partner zoo hires a worker, but the summary does not specify a Map A last-worker reward.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2; Association worker supply; Map A bonuses.

answers.answer: 1. Flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II; it remains in its current slot. 2. Its improved action is available beginning with your next action, but it counts as upgraded for conditions immediately. 3. The current action keeps the strength and kind established at its start. 4. You cannot upgrade all five cards because there are four upgrade opportunities, one of which allows an alternative choice.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: remains in slot, next action, immediate condition status, four ways and cannot upgrade all.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draws/discards by strength 1 through 5+: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1. 2. A required discard may be either a newly drawn card or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables; required discard may be new or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. The seven animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. 2. Bears and Petting Zoo animals count as categories unless the effect explicitly excludes them; bears may also have herbivore or predator icons.
answers.evidence: Animal categories; Base glossary shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. Association II permits exactly 1 donation, only if you performed at least 1 Association task in that same action. No worker is needed for the donation. 2. Pay the smallest still-visible amount and cover that space with a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation. 3. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces except the last are covered, subsequent donations cost 12 and place no more tokens. Limit one donation per Association action.
answers.evidence: Association II donation: task prerequisite, token source, reward, cost ladder, repeatable final space.

answers.answer: 1. Count Animal and Sponsor upper-right icons; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left of Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards, plus partner-zoo continent and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; university reputation and hand-limit marks are benefits, not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; university clarification; card-text priority.

answers.answer: 1. A requirement for two water or rock spaces is met by two distinct adjacent terrain hexes; multiple edges touching the same hex count as one, and a larger region counts only hexes actually adjacent. 2. Connectedness of the terrain region does not multiply the count. Water/rock illustrations on tiles are decorative and provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.
answers.evidence: Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. Only playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting a Release project already in play does not. 2. Breeding Program projects 123–127 have the same requirement at all three reward spaces, so choose any available one that is unoccupied under normal support rules.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild; Breeding Program projects 123–127 same requirement, choose any available space.

answers.answer: 1. For X:Y, the left side X is the condition and the right side Y is the reward. 2. A condition without a number, or with “per,” pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with multiple thresholds, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: shared principles, X:Y effects.

answers.answer: 1. Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. 2. Isolated means having no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space has no neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. “Your zoo” includes your played cards, map and personal supply. 5. “Any zoo” includes these for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. Unique buildings must be placed when their Sponsor card is played; if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. 2. Use the matching tile, colored face up, rotate freely but do not flip, and follow ordinary placement and terrain requirements. No size-based construction payment is due. 3. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house animals and never count as water or rock spaces.
answers.evidence: Unique buildings: placement with Sponsor, tile orientation, no size-based payment, placement/terrain rules, not enclosures.

answers.answer: 1. Complete the Animals action, including moving its Action card to slot 1, before taking the granted named action; then use that Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. 2. A named action cannot be replaced with the X-token alternative. Determination grants any action and may choose the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action/Determination.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen project to hand; Dominance does the same for its named project. 2. Dominance has no effect if that named project is already in play. 3. Later play and support the obtained card through Association, placing it above the board; it does not join the setup base-project row below.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion/Dominance.

answers.answer: 1. Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving that card. 2. Clever puts the chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or 5; moving it to slot 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Boost/Clever.

answers.answer: 1. All affected zoos need at least 5 appeal for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering and Constriction. 2. The animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability; its new appeal normally need not count when choosing affected players. 3. If the multiplayer group prefers, use the solo-marked replacement text for interactive abilities without playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities: shared five-appeal eligibility; playing animal's appeal timing; optional alternative text.

answers.answer: 1. Constriction affects each other eligible zoo ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: one track ahead gives 1 token on slot 5; both gives 2 tokens on slots 4 and 5. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens may restore strength. 4. Return a token after acting, or without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Interactive Constriction: token slots, no stacking, strength loss, multiplier and removal.

answers.answer: 1. A Constriction-marked card at effective strength 0 or below cannot be used as a regular action unless enough X-tokens raise it to at least 1. 2. Instead, you may take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3; the X-token alternative is itself subject to the five-token holding limit.
answers.evidence: Constriction edge case: at effective strength zero or below, boost to 1, use X-token action, or wait until slot 3.

answers.answer: 1. Digging 2 gives up to two selections, and you decide again after each, so the choices may differ. 2. A display card discarded through Digging is replaced immediately: higher folders slide down and the deck fills folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2 and Digging.

answers.answer: 1. A Flock Animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. 3. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join the flock animal in that enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, free an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure; exact historical residents need not be tracked or proved.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification: host, repeat use, later non-flock exclusion, release and no historical tracking.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take a last-worker map reward if shown. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification.

answers.answer: 1. If Hunter reveals no Animal card, discard all revealed cards.
answers.evidence: Hunter X: with no Animal among revealed cards, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Hypnosis chooses among tied highest-appeal zoos with at least 5 appeal; if the highest-appeal zoo is yours, it has no effect. 2. Copy only a card in the target's slot 1, 2 or 3 and use its owner's upgraded/unupgraded side; other upgrade checks use your own cards. 3. Spend your own X-tokens. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction tokens on that card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis clarification: targets, copied side/slots, own X-tokens, card movement and tokens.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card (a bonus-tile Multiplier can go on any card). With one token, execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength and move the card only after both executions. 2. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Defer after-finishing effects until both executions are done. 3. A break caused by the first execution waits until the whole turn, including the second execution, is finished. 4. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier clarification: placement, sequential executions, X-tokens, delayed break, and return.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three executions, not four. 2. Each X-token boosts one execution. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix one X-token action with one regular action.
answers.evidence: Multiplier clarification: each additional token adds one execution; X-token alternative and no mixing.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking lets you place a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, only if your zoo has no Aviary and a legal site exists. 2. Other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for restricted-icon map spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking and Posturing ability clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. Your first, second and third Petting Zoo animals give 3, 6 and 9 appeal, respectively. 2. The single Petting Zoo holds at most 3 such animals. 3. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; ties let you choose. 2. Pilfering 2 separately selects a highest-appeal target and a most-conservation target, each with at least 5 appeal; ties are your choice and the conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation. 3. If all players have zero conservation, only the conservation-target part has no effect; the highest-appeal part still resolves normally. 4. If the same zoo leads both, pilfer from it twice. Self-targeting has no effect.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X clarification: targets, ties, eligibility, zero conservation, same target and self-target.

answers.answer: 1. The affected player chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. With no hand cards, they give 5 money; with less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, even zero. 3. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X clarification: target's choice, card exclusion, shortages and sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch tucks hand cards beneath the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard those tucked cards too, but keep the appeal already gained. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins your choices when you discard one card at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every remaining Final Scoring card, each subject to its own maximum of 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Scavenging shuffles the discard pile face down, draws randomly from it, makes the card's specified selection, then returns the discard pile face up. For Scavenging 3, draw 3 random cards, keep 1 and discard the others.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification and illustrated Scavenging 3.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation; drawing from the deck is not an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet may take display Sponsors regardless of reputation range; if none is present it has no effect. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Venom places tokens on the lowest-slot cards (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including when the card is the alternative X-token action. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token and at least one remains on your cards; if unable to pay, undo the turn and choose a different action. 4. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom clarification: placement, use, fee/undo, and break expiration.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities when played. 2. Supporting conservation projects requires strength 4 instead of 5. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation for having three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough counts prior project supports by the number of player tokens missing from the left edge of your zoo map and gives 2 appeal per support. 2. It gives 1 conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research gives 1 conservation for each two different continent/animal-category icons. 2. Each other player gets 2 money for each conservation point you gain from it.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon on play. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Final scoring grants 1 conservation for five different animal categories.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon on play. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk, subject to ordinary placement and spacing rules. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation for five or more kiosks.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon on play. 2. Per Australia icon played, you may tuck 1 hand card beneath this Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. Each card enters play with 2 supply tokens on it. When supporting a base project below the Association board, return exactly 1 token to count as any one icon; never spend both for one support. 2. Base-origin cards later played above the board do not qualify. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation for five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 215/218 Global Breeding Program/Breeding Program.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer permits each Build action to add one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength. 2. Pay its normal cost and follow placement rules; special enclosures still have a one-per-type limit, and only one extra building is allowed even if several different buildings are built. 3. Final scoring gives 5 appeal with full map coverage except water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 217 Engineer.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon on play. 2. It lets you cover water/rock spaces and ignore animals' and unique buildings' terrain requirements; the printed terrain icons still count. 3. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo; terrain need not be covered for full-map completion. 4. Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, maximum 3 pairs.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Archaeologist triggers when an actual placement bonus on a border space is gained. 2. For each such bonus, choose any uncovered placement bonus on your map, not necessarily on the border; multiple triggers may choose the same or different bonuses, in any chosen order. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation if all building border spaces are covered, excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 221 Archaeologist.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token on play. 2. Each Release into the Wild support gives 1 additional conservation. You may support the same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, but place at most 1 token per project per Association action. 3. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token on play. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering; for Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3. Final scoring gives 1 conservation for having all five continents.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently, mark that choice with a supply player token, and reveal deck cards until finding an animal of that size; keep it and discard the rest. 2. You may not play animals of the opposite size. 3. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal and chosen large animals 4; size-3 animals remain legal but get no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 227 WAZA Special Assignment.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal on play. 2. An Animals action containing only small animals may play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs/rules. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the extra play. Mixing small and large animals in the original action prevents the effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon on play. 2. Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even when several belong to the same building; adjacency to several water hexes still pays only once per space. 3. Final scoring grants 1 conservation if all water hexes are connected (none isolated).
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut places its unique building. 2. Each bird icon played triggers drawing 2 deck cards, keeping 1 and discarding the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 249 Barred Owl Hut.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank places its unique building adjacent to water. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to 2 hand cards for 4 money each; discard the sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. Spotted Hyena Compound places its unique building. 2. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter, with the number of draws equal to your total predator icons. A card with two predator icons triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 252 Spotted Hyena Compound.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable places its building and 3 supply tokens on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor's level to play that Sponsor, meeting its normal conditions. 3. Playing the Stable can trigger its own effect if its herbivore icon applies; it has three uses total. 4. The Sponsor must come from hand.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 253 Okapi Stable; card text says hand Sponsor.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation on play. 2. Place its unique building covering at least 2 border spaces. 3. Take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; resolve simultaneous benefits in your chosen order.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance may be placed on 2 border spaces without touching an existing building; other placement rules apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. It gives 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may be next to a kiosk. 3. It is not itself a building for kiosk income. 4. Final scoring grants 5 appeal for full map coverage excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building-border space, never water or rock. 2. Final scoring gives 1 conservation per 6 contiguous empty building spaces; evaluate each group separately and sum completed groups. 3. Count restricted/upgrade-marked spaces even if Build is not upgraded; terrain spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon; research does not count. 2. Each category/continent newly introduced to your zoo gives 1 appeal and 2 money. 3. A double of the same new icon grants the novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program allows a free size-5 standard enclosure under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, including one required icon or the Animals upgrade, but not terrain requirements. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference 263 WAZA Large Animal Program.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your animal-category icon count with the player to your right and grants 1 conservation for each category where you have more icons. 2. If they have none of a category, one of your icons is enough. 3. Maximum 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo (009).

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower's bonus applies to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify, and the tower is not a building for kiosk income. 3. Housing an animal there gives the two appeal again even if an earlier animal was released and the enclosure emptied.
answers.evidence: Map 1 Observation Tower clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex, not merely another water hex. 2. Treat that enclosure as two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; a physical size-2 enclosure there counts as size 4. 3. Do not ignore this on release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and the Outdoor Area is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2 Outdoor Areas clarification.

answers.answer: 1. A building on Commercial Harbor's adjacent building space activates it; your first building may start beside the Harbor, but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used before, during or after your action, once per own turn, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4 Commercial Harbor clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant break income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless of building type or occupancy, and multiple hexes of one building count separately. 2. The Restaurant is not a building for kiosk income. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus grants one free Reptile House or one free Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5 Park Restaurant clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Cover each H space with a building under ordinary placement rules; when covered, reveal deck cards until a Sponsor appears, keep it and discard the others. 2. H is not a placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all 3 are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Its bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II for restricted spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8 Hollywood Hills clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual play conditions. 2. Play it only from hand, even with Sponsors II. 3. This paid-Sponsor bonus does not move the Sponsors Action card; it stays in its current slot.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: bonus letting you pay money to play a Sponsor.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; any gains beyond those track ends are lost.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: appeal and conservation track limits.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, subject to the 5-appeal minimum. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal (choose ties), has no effect if that is you, and copies only slots 1–3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal; Pilfering 2 separately targets highest appeal and most conservation; each target must have at least 5 appeal, ties are chosen by the actor, and self-targeting has no effect. A conservation target must have at least 1 point. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of you on appeal and/or conservation: one token if ahead on one, two tokens if ahead on both.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and Venom/Hypnosis/Pilfering/Constriction clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. An Animal partner-zoo condition requires a partner from the animal's specified continent; a Sponsor partner-zoo condition permits a partner from any continent. 2. A left-side maximum-25 appeal condition allows play only while appeal is at most 25; the marker is not a general cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. An ignore-one-condition bonus removes one left-edge requirement, but not terrain requirements.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: partner-zoo, max appeal, minimum reputation and ignore-one-condition rules.

answers.answer: 1. Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 offers up to two selections, choosing each time between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing a deck card. 2. After each selection you may choose either option again. A display discard is replaced immediately, sliding higher folders down and filling folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarification: Digging 2 and Digging.

answers.answer: 1. After a turn taking display cards, move cards from higher-numbered folders down, preserving their order, then fill the final empty folders from the deck. 2. On a break, discard folders 1 and 2, move remaining cards down and refill.
answers.evidence: Cards action: after display cards are taken, move higher folders down (keeping order) and fill empty spaces; break step 4 similarly compacts and refills.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each covered placement-bonus icon is gained immediately once, before the next building; flipping an enclosure occupied later does not award those bonuses again.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: standard enclosure orientation and placement bonuses.

answers.answer: 1. When the first player reaches or passes 10 conservation, every player chooses one Final Scoring card, places it face down under the remaining pile, and discards it there.
answers.evidence: Scoring during the game: all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turns proceed clockwise. 2. Play has no formal rounds; players take turns until the end is triggered, with breaks in between. 3. Each turn has one regular action using one Action card; then move cards and resolve any after-finishing effects, with additional actions/bonuses from effects resolved as specified.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine start player, clockwise; Overview: no formal rounds; Turn Structure: one action each turn.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before game end, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
answers.evidence: Scoring during the game: if nobody reaches 10, all discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring.
